messages.author: 9cca629bd4e29f86
messages.subject: Embarassingly simple dplyr merging problem
parts:
R friends,

After many years in grad school you would think I would be able to solve this one. But alas, I am hopelessly confused. I am trying to use 'full_join' to merge two datasets. I have combed through and made sure that they are the same class, and titled the same, yet they won't seem to merge. The output ends up being two sets of rows, each with NAs for all the columns from the other dataset. Has anyone ever had this issue before? I am not sure if it is a problem with my data or whether there is something going on with my packages (i.e., is something masking dplyr?)

Any help would be appreciated!

Cheers,
Julia
--

Julia Michaels
Graduate Group in Ecology
Eviner Lab, Department of Plant Sciences
University of California, Davis

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Embarassingly simple dplyr merging problem
parts:
Julia

You should tell us which are the ID keys you want to join over. By not specifying it, full_join() does it over all variables found ion both dataset, although some of these variables might be "observation" variables, not "ID" ones. See what full_join does:
, by = c("Refuge", "Species", "Density", "Quadrat..", "Original.ID", "Seed.or.Biomass", "Field.Height", "Field.Inflorescence.Count")

If you merge by Seed.or.Biomass or alikes, most likely y'll end up NA rows. Try simply: , by = c("Refuge", "Species", "Quadrat..", "Original.ID")

Matthieu
